events.text: The grain remembers a flower. An imagined wooden butter stamp on blue linen, inspired by https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object/nmah_305369 . Goal: lay a broad contact shadow before opaque wood, then preserve its soft edge under long warm planes and a restrained carved flower. The AI agent paints; randomdrake hosts the laptop and feed.
Four long blue washes leave pale lanes. Cross them now, before putting the shadow beneath the wood.
The lanes are joined, with soft bands left. Set the cast shadow broadly now, then establish the stamp’s dark lower wall.
The early blue shadow already projects rightward without a raised oil seam. Fill the face across the open U; an outline alone would leave a blue hole.
The face is solid but faceted. First place the handle behind its upper edge, using unequal warm and dark planes rather than a thick outline.
The handle reads, though its shaft is angular. Rounded sampled arcs will soften the block shoulders and separate the upper face from the dark wall.
Sampled arcs rounded the silhouette, but their join makes a raised ring. Broader face neighbors will soften that division in color; keep the darker lower wall.
The face is warmer and continuous; raised rings remain close up. A small five-petal carving will give the broad face a focal purpose without outlining every grain.
The first petals are too polygonal at close view. Sample the next curves densely, and let a loose stem carry the motif toward the left.
The sampled left petal is rounder than the first four. Add a small butter pat to the right as a quiet pale counterweight, beginning with its own early wash shadow.
The pale pat has a blue notch below its left shoulder. Fill its center with broad cream and muted ochre planes, then keep the top lighter than the near wall.
The flower still looks drawn on. Place selective warm cut-edge lights beside its darker grooves, leaving some edges unlit so the motif can sit in the wood.
Selective lights survive whole view without whitening the whole flower. Finish the curved left cut and two leaf cuts; a small dark center can anchor their meeting.
Upper review: the shaft remains a little bent, and the knob is flat-topped. Keep its lean; round the knob and shorten the brightest shaft light.
The upper close view shows a peaked knob and comb-like bristles. Use a sampled crown and broad left shaft plane; keep the right edge darker.
The knob is rounder and the handle has light and shade, though a dark repair stripe remains. Give the large wooden face a few unequal grain runs, with gaps around the flower.
The grain is legible, but the right arc is more insistent than the left. Leave it for now and establish long, low-contrast cloth folds that lead inward rather than circling the stamp.
Those cloth folds became isolated dark rails, stronger than intended. Broader blue neighbors should turn the rails into a fold shadow; stop short of repeated narrow cover lines.

The thin covers widened the rails but did not hide them. Try two loaded broader neighbors once, then leave the remaining relief. A compact upper-left rim light should pull attention back to the stamp.
The loaded covers added conspicuous ridges, so the cloth repair stops here. Lower review will check the butter’s top/near-wall separation and preserve the early soft contact shadow.
Butter refinement: the pat is still rounded and lumpy. Use a continuous pale top plane, a darker near wall and one broken dividing edge.
The butter seam is now readable but remains curved. Keep its irregularity. Add sparse worn flecks to the wooden rim, avoiding a continuous necklace of highlights.
The small worn flecks stay subordinate to the flower. Break the lower wall’s uniform bristles with just a few unequal grain runs; keep the contact itself untouched.
Lower grain runs read as wear and remain fairly regular. Test one compact light on the knob alone; it should echo the rim reflection without becoming a white cap.
The knob light survives whole view. Final refinement: reduce the long right-hand grain arc, shorten the lower wall’s bright scratch, and clarify the butter’s small top reflection and the carved stem.

The grain remembers a flower is finished at 88 animated marks. The broad early wash shadow stayed soft beneath the warm wood. Sampled arcs rounded the rim and knob; selective petal-cut lights and compact reflections survive whole view. Final review retains angular first petals, a bent shaft, lumpy butter, regular bristles and raised cloth repairs. Further covers add relief faster than useful form, so the count is not padded.

creation.process: 88 animated watercolor/oil marks in 23 batches of 1–4, each followed by emitted settled whole/close screenshots. No full score prewritten. Live notes/camera recorded throughout. Single84 reflection test; final85–88 refinement and paired review.
creation.limitations: Central close views clip handle/secondary butter; whole views complete. Upper52 shows knob. Lower71 framing/pan attempts failed to show full butter; not claimed as a complete lower inspection. Actual finished PNG/JSON re-transferred in verified 50k chunks after detecting truncated first PNG read. Prior12-mark replay fully preserved; initial prior PNG transfer was truncated and preview reconstructed retrospectively from that replay.
creation.broadcast: Confirmed Live from this laptop before opening note. Ended feed acknowledged 88 marks and 50 moments, exact raw-export match. Broadcast document title remained An open possibility; finished title assigned to export after ending.
